audit.title: Supported Networks for Report Verification

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The lead answers the implied question conceptually — "supports onchain report verification on all networks where Data Streams verifier contracts are available" — but stops short of naming any network, so a lifted chunk still leaves the reader without the concrete answer.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1→H2 hierarchy, 0 level skips, short coherent sections. Weak point: no table or bulleted network list on a page whose title demands one.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 numerals, 0 hex identifiers, 0 network names. This is the single worst dimension and the most damaging for a "supported networks" page.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 4 internal links to the right canonical pages (verifier-proxy-addresses, onchain-verification, data-streams); no external/primary sources, acceptable for a hub page.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: "DataLink uses the same infrastructure and Verifier Proxy contracts as Chainlink Data Streams" is crisp and liftable — good.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dateModified. Head could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` — but nothing was detected.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code; largely acceptable for a pointer page, but a single Verifier Proxy address example would raise concreteness.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Addresses "how does verification work" but does not enumerate networks or cover symptom queries; the core intent (list of chains) is deferred entirely.

audit.summary: This is a short navigational hub page that explains DataLink reuses Chainlink Data Streams' Verifier Proxy contracts for onchain verification, then routes users to the actual address list and tutorial. Its biggest strength is a clean, quotable canonical statement ("DataLink uses the same infrastructure and Verifier Proxy contracts as Chainlink Data Streams"). Its biggest liability is that a page titled *Supported Networks* lists **zero networks** — it contains no chain names, no chain IDs, no addresses, and no metadata — so it will lose retrieval for "what networks does DataLink support" to the very page it links to. Honest verdict: clear prose, but too thin and specifics-free to earn citations for its own title query.

recommendations.title: Embed a supported-networks summary table on the page itself
recommendations.issue: "Find the list of supported networks... on the [Verifier Proxy Addresses] page." — the page delegates its entire titular content.
recommendations.change: Add a table with columns Network · Chain ID · Verifier Proxy Address (mainnet + testnet rows), even if abbreviated, with a link to the full list. At minimum list the network names in prose.
recommendations.why: A page titled "Supported Networks" with zero networks and zero numerals cannot win its own query; concrete chain names/IDs/addresses are among the highest-lift additions and prevent the linked page from outranking this one.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/question-phrased heading and answer-first line
recommendations.issue: No heading matches "What networks does DataLink support?" — the query users actually type.
recommendations.change: Add an H2 "What networks does DataLink support for onchain verification?" opening with the direct answer ("DataLink supports onchain verification on every network where Chainlink Data Streams verifier contracts are deployed, including [list]").
recommendations.why: Concept-titled prose loses retrieval that question-phrased headings win, even when the answer is present.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema, canonical URL, and dateModified
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, dateModified absent.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, canonical `url`, and `inLanguage`; add a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent parseability and E-E-A-T trust; note this is likely a site-wide template fix, not page-specific.

recommendations.title: Add one concrete Verifier Proxy address example inline
recommendations.issue: "using the Verifier Proxy contract on the relevant chain" — no address shown.
recommendations.change: Include one labeled example, e.g. a fenced snippet showing a network name + `0x…` Verifier Proxy address, tagged with the network.
recommendations.why: Hex identifiers and concrete params raise extractability and let agents complete the verification task without a second hop.

antiPatterns: Thin routing page: nearly all substantive content (the actual network list) is deferred via links, leaving the page unable to answer its own title query.
No dated/freshness signal on a page listing network support, which changes over time.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD/`TechArticle`, canonical, and `inLanguage` are almost certainly site-template concerns — fix once at the layout level.
`llms.txt` is already referenced in the page — good; ensure this URL is indexed there.
Head metadata could not be verified from the supplied content; pass raw `<head>` to the CLI for a definitive metadata read.
